reviewed: analyses/M737_g0.json against analyses/M737_spec.md Rev 2; blind audit analyses/M737_audit.json (accept)
decision: accept: G0 ends M737 as 'not testable at this support' (R1/R2); not a falsification of DEM grade; no owner sign-off needed
required_fixes: tool writes the support count without the ratio screen (done: 9 days, 26 drives, below 30, so the outcome does not depend on the post-hoc screen)
deviations block written by the tool and repeated in the CHANGELOG (done)
CHANGELOG entry with the spec Rev 2 sha256, master MD5 before and after, audit verdict and this decision (done); spec text unchanged
wording: not testable at this support (8 days < 30-day floor)
never DEM grade rejected, falsified or failed
cloud-minus-OBD position disagreement, not cloud accuracy
+16 s is the best-agreeing shift, not a latency
logged GPS altitude is a proxy reference; DEM or route grade is estimated, never measured
the valid-track subset (400 of 627 drives) is selected on OBD speed consistency
retest_rule: not an ingestion stage; docs/open_items.md item: run the offline G0 support count at each ingestion; re-run G0 under Rev 2 when qualifying segments cover at least 30 days or the logger altitude column is routinely populated; freeze the ratio screen and speed-class rule as a Rev 3 addendum before any re-run; G2 runs once, only after Andrii approves the downloads
risks: altitude is logged in bursts on few days and does not cover the steepest driving (R5), so 30 days may take long or never happen
the post-hoc screen drops about a third of drives and could bias a later P2 unless frozen first
tool and auditor differ by 7 to 18 m on P1 and by about 134 segments on P2 because rules were ambiguous; both far below the floor
cloud spacing above 80 km/h (median about 870 m) exceeds L=500 m, so P2b at high speed may stay unmatched even with enough support
